intro: You already join ideas with **but**, **because** and **so**. In this lesson you'll sound more grown-up in emails, reports and conversations: **although** and **however** for a surprise (contrast), **because of** and **due to** for reasons, and **to**, **in order to** and **so that** for goals. Warm-up: why are you learning English? Finish the sentence: I'm learning English so that I can …
teachingNotes: Recap first, in one line: from a1-conjunctions and a2-linkers-sequence the learner knows but (tapi), because (karena) + subject + verb, and so (jadi) for a result, plus the rule 'one linker per sentence' (*'Because it rained, so I stayed home'). This lesson adds the more formal linkers. Explain 'clause' as 'subject + verb' (siapa + melakukan apa: it was late, Budi took a taxi) and 'noun' as 'kata benda' (the rain, a problem, the traffic) the first time: the whole lesson rests on this difference.

Contrast: although / even though (meskipun / walaupun) + subject + verb. Either part can come first; comma only when the although-part is first. even though is the same idea but stronger (more surprise). The node's common error comes from Indonesian 'Meskipun …, tetapi …': *'Although it was raining, but we went out'. One sentence takes although OR but, never both (same rule as 'Karena …, jadi …'). Also *'Although the rain, …': although needs a subject + verb. despite / in spite of (+ noun) are NOT taught here: if asked, give one example and say it comes later.

however (namun) starts a NEW sentence and has a comma after it: The hotel was cheap. However, it was clean. It can't join two parts like but: *'The hotel was cheap, however it was clean' is a common writing mistake. Indonesian 'Namun, …' works the same way, which helps. 'The rooms, however, were clean' (however in the middle) is correct: accept it, don't teach it. Don't teach '; however,' or however = bagaimanapun (however hard I try). 'But' at the start of a sentence is fine in informal writing: don't mark it wrong, don't test it.

Reason: because + subject + verb (because it was raining) vs because of / due to + noun (because of the rain, due to the rain). Indonesian 'karena' covers both, which causes the node's error *'Because of it was late, I took a taxi'. Quick test: is there a verb after the linker? Yes → because; only a noun → because of / due to. due to is more formal: notices, announcements, news, work emails (The KRL is late due to a technical problem). because of + a pronoun (because of you) is fine. Don't teach because of + -ing, owing to, as / since for reasons, or 'the delay was due to …' as a separate rule (accept it).

Purpose: to + base verb (recap from a2-verb-patterns: I went to the bank to get cash); in order to + base verb = the same, a bit more formal; so that + subject + can / could / will (so that I can, so that she could). Use could after a past verb (I left early so that I could get a seat). The node's common error is Indonesian 'untuk' → *'I study hard for pass the exam': for + noun (for the exam) is fine, for + verb is not. Second trap: so that = supaya / agar (a goal, the plan), while so = jadi (a result, what happened): 'It rained, so we went inside', not *'so that we went inside'. In speech 'so I can' often means so that: accept it, but practise with that. Don't teach so as to, in order not to or in order that.

Grammar limits: present simple and continuous, past simple and continuous, present perfect, will, going to, can/could and should/must are fine. No passive (avoid 'was cancelled / is delayed' in examples: use 'is late', 'didn't happen', 'is closed'), no past perfect, no second conditional, no reported speech. Real contexts: KRL, ojek online, office in Jakarta, TOEIC, saving money, flights to Bali, rain and floods. Correct one thing at a time, usually the double linker or the because/because of choice.

keyPoints.title: Contrast: although, even though, however
keyPoints.explanation: although and even though (meskipun / walaupun) + subject + verb show a surprise: Although the KRL was crowded, I got a seat. even though is stronger. Use although OR but, never both: not 'Although …, but …'. however (namun) starts a new sentence, with a comma after it: The hotel was cheap. However, it was clean. It can't join two parts like but.

examples.en: Although the KRL was crowded, I got a seat.
examples.id: Meskipun KRL-nya penuh, saya dapat tempat duduk.

examples.en: Even though Budi was sick, he went to work.
examples.id: Walaupun Budi sakit, dia tetap masuk kerja.

examples.en: The hotel was cheap. However, it was very clean.
examples.id: Hotelnya murah. Namun, hotelnya sangat bersih.

id.title: Kontras: although, even though, however
id.explanation: although dan even though (meskipun / walaupun) + subjek + kata kerja menunjukkan hal yang mengejutkan: Although the KRL was crowded, I got a seat. even though lebih kuat. Pakai although ATAU but, jangan dua-duanya: bukan 'Although …, but …'. however (namun) memulai kalimat baru, dengan koma setelahnya: The hotel was cheap. However, it was clean. however tidak bisa menyambung dua bagian kalimat seperti but.

keyPoints.title: Reasons: because + subject + verb, because of / due to + noun
keyPoints.explanation: Indonesian karena has two English forms. If a subject + verb comes next, use because: because it was raining. If only a noun (kata benda) comes next, use because of or due to: because of the rain, due to the rain. due to is more formal (notices, news, work emails). Not 'Because of it was late'.

examples.en: I took an ojek because it was late.
examples.id: Saya naik ojek karena sudah malam.

examples.en: The football match stopped because of the rain.
examples.id: Pertandingan sepak bolanya berhenti karena hujan.

examples.en: The KRL is late due to a technical problem.

id.title: Alasan: because + subjek + kata kerja, because of / due to + kata benda
id.explanation: Kata karena punya dua bentuk dalam bahasa Inggris. Kalau setelahnya ada subjek + kata kerja, pakai because: because it was raining. Kalau setelahnya hanya kata benda, pakai because of atau due to: because of the rain, due to the rain. due to lebih formal (pengumuman, berita, email kantor). Bukan 'Because of it was late'.

keyPoints.title: Purpose: to, in order to, so that
keyPoints.explanation: To say why you do something (your goal), use to or in order to + a base verb (go, buy, pass): I'm saving money to buy a laptop. in order to is a bit more formal. Or use so that + subject + can / could / will: I left early so that I could get a seat. Indonesian untuk is not for + verb: not 'for pass the exam'. And so that (supaya) is not so (jadi).

examples.en: Sari is saving money to buy a laptop.
We are hiring more staff in order to open a new branch.
examples.id: Kami merekrut lebih banyak karyawan untuk membuka cabang baru.

examples.en: I left early so that I could get a seat on the KRL.
examples.id: Saya berangkat lebih awal supaya bisa dapat tempat duduk di KRL.

id.title: Tujuan: to, in order to, so that
id.explanation: Untuk mengatakan kenapa kamu melakukan sesuatu (tujuanmu), pakai to atau in order to + kata kerja dasar (go, buy, pass): I'm saving money to buy a laptop. in order to sedikit lebih formal. Atau pakai so that + subjek + can / could / will: I left early so that I could get a seat. Kata untuk bukan for + kata kerja: bukan 'for pass the exam'. Dan so that (supaya) berbeda dengan so (jadi).

assessment.prompt: Keep although and correct the mistake: Although the hotel was expensive, but the room was small and dirty.
acceptableAnswers: although the hotel was expensive the room was small and dirty
the room was small and dirty although the hotel was expensive
assessment.rubric: Correct: Although the hotel was expensive, the room was small and dirty (remove but: one sentence takes although OR but). 'Even though the hotel was expensive, the room was small and dirty' = 100. 'The hotel was expensive, but the room was small and dirty' = 60 (correct English, but the task said keep although). Unchanged or 'However' added = 0.

assessment.prompt: Write although or however: The apartment is near my office. ___, the rent is very high.
acceptableAnswers: however
assessment.rubric: Correct: However (a full stop before the gap and a comma after it: However starts a new sentence). 'Although' = 0 (although needs a subject + verb after it in the same sentence and is never followed by a comma). 'But' = 30 (it can start a sentence in informal writing, but not with a comma after it, and it isn't one of the two choices).

assessment.prompt: Write because or because of: Dimas missed the meeting ___ a problem with his laptop.
acceptableAnswers: because of
due to
assessment.rubric: Correct: because of (only a noun follows: a problem with his laptop; there's no verb). 'due to' = 100 (also right, more formal). 'because' = 0 (because needs a subject + verb after it).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: Because of the KRL was late, I missed the meeting.
acceptableAnswers: because the krl was late i missed the meeting
i missed the meeting because the krl was late
because of the late krl i missed the meeting
assessment.rubric: Correct: Because the KRL was late, I missed the meeting (a subject + verb follows, so because, not because of). 'Because of the late KRL, I missed the meeting' = 100 (because of + a noun). 'Due to the KRL was late' = 0 (same mistake). Unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: An airport announcement needs a more formal word. Rewrite the sentence with due to: The flight to Bali is late because the weather is bad.
acceptableAnswers: the flight to bali is late due to the bad weather
the flight to bali is late due to bad weather
the flight to bali's late due to bad weather
the flight to bali's late due to the bad weather
due to bad weather the flight to bali is late
due to the bad weather the flight to bali is late
assessment.rubric: Correct: The flight to Bali is late due to (the) bad weather (due to + a noun phrase, so 'the weather is bad' becomes 'bad weather'). 'due to the weather' = 70 (right pattern, but 'bad' is lost). 'due to the weather is bad' = 0 (due to can't take a subject + verb). 'because of bad weather' = 50 (right pattern, but not due to).

assessment.prompt: Keep the verb buy and correct the mistake: Rina is saving money for buy a new motorbike.
acceptableAnswers: rina is saving money to buy a new motorbike
rina's saving money to buy a new motorbike
rina is saving money in order to buy a new motorbike
rina's saving money in order to buy a new motorbike
rina is saving money so that she can buy a new motorbike
rina's saving money so that she can buy a new motorbike
assessment.rubric: Correct: Rina is saving money to buy a new motorbike (purpose = to / in order to + base verb; untuk is not for + verb). 'so that she can buy' = 100. 'for buying' = 30 (still for before a verb). 'to buying' = 40. Unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Fill the gap with so that + a subject + can: Budi leaves home at 5 a.m. ___ catch the first KRL.
acceptableAnswers: so that he can
assessment.rubric: Correct: so that he can (so that + subject + can + verb). 'so he can' = 70 (fine in speech, but the task asked for so that). 'so that can' or 'so that he' = 30 (subject or can missing). 'in order to' or 'to' = 40 (right idea, but not the pattern asked for). 'so that he could' = 60 (could is for the past; this is a habit).

material.title: although / even though: a surprise in one sentence

blocks.text:
You know **but** (tapi): *The food was cheap, **but** it was delicious.* Now meet **although** and **even though** = *meskipun / walaupun*. They show a **contrast**: the second idea is a surprise after the first.

After although you need a **clause**: a **subject** (who or what: *I, Budi, the KRL*) + a **verb** (*was, rained, works*). *Although **the KRL was** crowded, I got a seat.*
- The although-part can come first (then put a **comma** after it) or second (no comma): *I got a seat although the KRL was crowded.*
- **even though** is the same idea, but stronger: more surprise. *Even though Budi was sick, he went to work.*
- Although needs a subject + verb: not `Although the rain, we went out`. Say *Although it was raining, …*.

id.text:
Kamu sudah tahu **but** (tapi): *The food was cheap, **but** it was delicious.* Sekarang kenalan dengan **although** dan **even though** = *meskipun / walaupun*. Keduanya menunjukkan **kontras**: ide kedua mengejutkan setelah ide pertama.

Setelah although harus ada **klausa** (clause): **subjek** (siapa atau apa: *I, Budi, the KRL*) + **kata kerja** (*was, rained, works*). *Although **the KRL was** crowded, I got a seat.* (Meskipun KRL-nya penuh, saya dapat tempat duduk.)
- Bagian although bisa di depan (lalu beri **koma** setelahnya) atau di belakang (tanpa koma): *I got a seat although the KRL was crowded.*
- **even though** artinya sama, tapi lebih kuat: lebih mengejutkan. *Even though Budi was sick, he went to work.* (Walaupun sakit, Budi tetap masuk kerja.)
- although butuh subjek + kata kerja: bukan `Although the rain, we went out`. Katakan *Although it was raining, …*.

blocks.text: Indonesian trap: **Meskipun …, tetapi …**. In Indonesian many people use both words. In English, one sentence takes **although OR but**, never both: `Although it was raining, but we went out` is wrong. Say *Although it was raining, we went out* or *It was raining, but we went out*. It's the same rule you learnt for *Karena …, jadi …* (because OR so).

id.text: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: **Meskipun …, tetapi …**. Dalam bahasa Indonesia banyak orang memakai dua kata itu sekaligus. Dalam bahasa Inggris, satu kalimat memakai **although ATAU but**, jangan dua-duanya: `Although it was raining, but we went out` salah. Katakan *Although it was raining, we went out* atau *It was raining, but we went out*. Ini aturan yang sama dengan *Karena …, jadi …* yang sudah kamu pelajari (because ATAU so).

options: Although Sari studied hard, but she failed the test.
Although Sari studied hard, she failed the test.
Although Sari's hard study, she failed the test.
blocks.explain: **although** + subject + verb (*Sari studied*), a comma, then the other part with **no but**. The first sentence uses two linkers (the *Meskipun …, tetapi …* trap). The third has no verb after although.

id.explain: **although** + subjek + kata kerja (*Sari studied*), koma, lalu bagian lainnya **tanpa but**. Kalimat pertama memakai dua kata penghubung (jebakan *Meskipun …, tetapi …*). Kalimat ketiga tidak punya kata kerja setelah although.

id.title: although / even though: kejutan dalam satu kalimat

material.title: however: a new sentence, with a comma

blocks.text:
**however** = *namun*. It also shows a contrast, but it works differently: it **starts a new sentence**, after a full stop, and it has a **comma** after it.

*The hotel was cheap. **However,** it was very clean.*

You can't use however to join two parts inside one sentence like but: `The hotel was cheap, however it was clean` is a very common writing mistake. Inside one sentence, use **but** or **although**. however is a little formal: you'll see it in emails, reports and news.

Good news: Indonesian **Namun, …** works the same way. If you'd write *Namun,* at the start of a sentence, write **However,**.

id.text:
**however** = *namun*. Kata ini juga menunjukkan kontras, tapi cara pakainya berbeda: however **memulai kalimat baru**, setelah titik, dan ada **koma** setelahnya.

*The hotel was cheap. **However,** it was very clean.* (Hotelnya murah. Namun, hotelnya sangat bersih.)

Kamu tidak bisa memakai however untuk menyambung dua bagian di dalam satu kalimat seperti but: `The hotel was cheap, however it was clean` adalah kesalahan menulis yang sangat umum. Di dalam satu kalimat, pakai **but** atau **although**. however sedikit formal: kamu akan melihatnya di email, laporan dan berita.

Kabar baiknya: **Namun, …** dalam bahasa Indonesia bekerja dengan cara yang sama. Kalau kamu akan menulis *Namun,* di awal kalimat, tulis **However,**.

rows.en: The hotel was cheap. However, it was very clean.
rows.id: Hotelnya murah. Namun, hotelnya sangat bersih.

rows.en: The hotel was cheap, but it was very clean.
rows.id: Hotelnya murah, tapi sangat bersih.

rows.en: We planned to finish on Friday. However, the client changed the design.

rows.en: Prices went up last month. However, sales were still good.
rows.id: Harga naik bulan lalu. Namun, penjualan tetap bagus.

blocks.text: Quick test for the gap: is there a **full stop before** it and a **comma right after** it? Then it's **However,**. Is it in the middle of one sentence, joining two parts? Then use **but** (or put **although** at the start of one part). You may also see however in the middle (*The rooms, however, were small*): that's correct too, but you don't need it yet.

id.text: Tes cepat untuk titik-titiknya: apakah ada **titik sebelumnya** dan **koma tepat setelahnya**? Berarti **However,**. Apakah ada di tengah satu kalimat, menyambung dua bagian? Pakai **but** (atau taruh **although** di awal salah satu bagian). Kamu mungkin juga melihat however di tengah (*The rooms, however, were small*): itu juga benar, tapi belum perlu kamu pakai.

blocks.prompt: Complete: Our team worked late every night. ___, we didn't finish the project on time.
blocks.explain: There's a full stop before the gap and a comma after it, so a new sentence starts: **However,**. *Although* needs a subject + verb after it in the same sentence, and *Because of* needs a noun and gives a reason, not a surprise.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Our team worked late every night. ___, we didn't finish the project on time.
id.explain: Ada titik sebelum titik-titiknya dan koma setelahnya, jadi kalimat baru dimulai: **However,**. *Although* butuh subjek + kata kerja setelahnya dalam kalimat yang sama, dan *Because of* butuh kata benda dan memberi alasan, bukan kejutan.

material.title: karena: because, because of or due to?

blocks.text:
Indonesian **karena** has two English forms. Look at **what comes right after it**:
- a **subject + verb** (a clause: *it was late, the road was busy*) → **because**: *I took an ojek **because it was** late.*
- only a **noun** (kata benda: a thing or idea, like *the rain, the traffic, a problem*) → **because of** or **due to**: *The match stopped **because of the rain**.*

So *karena hujan* can be *because it was raining* (subject + verb) or *because of the rain* (noun). Both are right; just don't mix them: `Because of it was late` is wrong.

**due to** means the same as because of, but it's more **formal**: you'll hear it in KRL and airport announcements, read it in notices and the news, and use it in work emails. *The KRL is late due to a technical problem.*

id.text:
Kata **karena** punya dua bentuk dalam bahasa Inggris. Lihat **apa yang langsung datang setelahnya**:
- **subjek + kata kerja** (klausa: *it was late, the road was busy*) → **because**: *I took an ojek **because it was** late.* (Saya naik ojek karena sudah malam.)
- hanya **kata benda** (noun: benda atau hal, seperti *the rain, the traffic, a problem*) → **because of** atau **due to**: *The match stopped **because of the rain**.* (Pertandingannya berhenti karena hujan.)

Jadi *karena hujan* bisa *because it was raining* (subjek + kata kerja) atau *because of the rain* (kata benda). Dua-duanya benar; asal jangan dicampur: `Because of it was late` salah.

**due to** artinya sama dengan because of, tapi lebih **formal**: kamu akan mendengarnya di pengumuman KRL dan bandara, membacanya di pengumuman dan berita, dan memakainya di email kantor. *The KRL is late due to a technical problem.* (KRL terlambat karena gangguan teknis.)

rows.id: Kami di rumah saja karena hujan.

rows.en: We stayed home because of the rain.
rows.id: Kami di rumah saja karena hujan.

rows.en: The KRL is late due to a technical problem.
rows.id: KRL terlambat karena gangguan teknis.

rows.en: Many people work from home because of the traffic.

blocks.text: The verb test: after the gap, can you find a **verb** (*is, was, rained, has*)? Yes → **because**. No, only a noun → **because of / due to**. And remember from earlier lessons: **because** gives the reason, **so** gives the result. Don't use both in one sentence.

id.text: Tes kata kerja: setelah titik-titiknya, apakah ada **kata kerja** (*is, was, rained, has*)? Ada → **because**. Tidak ada, hanya kata benda → **because of / due to**. Dan ingat dari pelajaran sebelumnya: **because** memberi alasan, **so** memberi akibat. Jangan pakai dua-duanya dalam satu kalimat.

blocks.prompt: Complete: Many flights to Surabaya are late today ___ the storm.
blocks.explain: Only a noun comes after the gap (*the storm*), with no verb, so use **due to** (or because of). *because* needs a subject + verb (*because there is a storm*). *so that* is for a goal, not a reason.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Many flights to Surabaya are late today ___ the storm.
id.explain: Setelah titik-titiknya hanya ada kata benda (*the storm*), tanpa kata kerja, jadi pakai **due to** (atau because of). *because* butuh subjek + kata kerja (*because there is a storm*). *so that* untuk tujuan, bukan alasan.

id.title: karena: because, because of atau due to?

material.title: untuk / supaya: to, in order to, so that

blocks.text:
A **purpose** is your goal: *why* you do something. You already know **to + verb** for this: *I went to the bank **to get** some cash.* Now two more ways:
- **in order to** + a **base verb** (the plain verb: *buy, pass, open*, no -s, -ing or -ed) = the same as to, but a bit more **formal**: *We are hiring more staff **in order to open** a new branch.*
- **so that** (*supaya / agar*) + **subject + can / could / will** + verb: *I'm saving money **so that I can** buy a laptop.* After a past verb, use **could**: *I left early **so that I could** get a seat.*

so that is useful when the person changes: *I'll send you the file **so that you can** check it.*

id.text:
**Tujuan** (purpose) adalah sasaranmu: *kenapa* kamu melakukan sesuatu. Kamu sudah tahu **to + kata kerja** untuk ini: *I went to the bank **to get** some cash.* (Saya ke bank untuk mengambil uang.) Sekarang ada dua cara lagi:
- **in order to** + **kata kerja dasar** (kata kerja polos: *buy, pass, open*, tanpa -s, -ing atau -ed) = sama dengan to, tapi sedikit lebih **formal**: *We are hiring more staff **in order to open** a new branch.* (Kami merekrut karyawan baru untuk membuka cabang baru.)
- **so that** (*supaya / agar*) + **subjek + can / could / will** + kata kerja: *I'm saving money **so that I can** buy a laptop.* (Saya menabung supaya bisa beli laptop.) Setelah kata kerja bentuk lampau, pakai **could**: *I left early **so that I could** get a seat.*

so that berguna kalau orangnya berganti: *I'll send you the file **so that you can** check it.* (Saya akan kirim filenya supaya kamu bisa memeriksanya.)

rows.en: I went to the bank to get some cash.
rows.id: Saya ke bank untuk mengambil uang tunai.

rows.en: Students must arrive early in order to register.
rows.id: Mahasiswa harus datang lebih awal untuk mendaftar.

rows.en: I'll send you the file so that you can check it.
rows.id: Saya akan kirim filenya supaya kamu bisa memeriksanya.

rows.en: I left early so that I could get a seat on the KRL.
rows.id: Saya berangkat lebih awal supaya bisa dapat tempat duduk di KRL.

rows.en: I study hard for the exam.
rows.id: Saya belajar keras untuk ujian.

blocks.text:
Two Indonesian traps.
- **untuk + verb is not for + verb**: `I study hard for pass the exam` is wrong. Say *to pass* or *in order to pass*. **for** goes before a noun: *for the exam*.
- **supaya is not jadi**: **so that** = a goal (*supaya*), **so** = a result, what happened (*jadi*). *It rained, **so** we went inside* (result), not `so that we went inside`. In conversation people often say *so I can* for a goal: that's fine, but write **so that**.

id.text:
Dua jebakan bahasa Indonesia.
- **untuk + kata kerja bukan for + kata kerja**: `I study hard for pass the exam` salah. Katakan *to pass* atau *in order to pass*. **for** dipakai sebelum kata benda: *for the exam*.
- **supaya bukan jadi**: **so that** = tujuan (*supaya*), **so** = akibat, apa yang terjadi (*jadi*). *It rained, **so** we went inside* (akibat), bukan `so that we went inside`. Dalam percakapan orang sering bilang *so I can* untuk tujuan: itu boleh, tapi kalau menulis pakai **so that**.

blocks.prompt: Complete: Dimas is learning Japanese ___ he can work in Tokyo next year.
blocks.explain: After the gap comes a subject + can (*he can work*), so use **so that**. *in order to* needs a base verb right after it (*in order to work*), and *for* never goes before a verb or a subject + verb.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Dimas is learning Japanese ___ he can work in Tokyo next year.
id.explain: Setelah titik-titiknya ada subjek + can (*he can work*), jadi pakai **so that**. *in order to* butuh kata kerja dasar langsung setelahnya (*in order to work*), dan *for* tidak pernah dipakai sebelum kata kerja atau subjek + kata kerja.

id.title: untuk / supaya: to, in order to, so that

blocks.text: Here is a short email from Bu Ani to her team. Find the **contrast** words (although, however), the **reasons** (because of, due to) and the **goals** (to, in order to, so that). Notice the punctuation around **However,**.

id.text: Ini email singkat dari Bu Ani untuk timnya. Temukan kata-kata **kontras** (although, however), **alasan** (because of, due to) dan **tujuan** (to, in order to, so that). Perhatikan tanda baca di sekitar **However,**.

rows.en: Hi team, the meeting with the client is now on Thursday due to a problem with their flight.
rows.id: Halo tim, rapat dengan klien sekarang hari Kamis karena ada masalah dengan penerbangan mereka.

rows.en: Although we have more time now, please finish your slides by Tuesday.
rows.id: Meskipun sekarang kita punya lebih banyak waktu, tolong selesaikan slide kalian paling lambat Selasa.

id.note: although + subjek + kata kerja, tanpa but

rows.en: I'd like to check them on Wednesday so that we can fix any mistakes.

rows.en: The office is closed on Friday because of the holiday. However, please check your email.
rows.id: Kantor tutup hari Jumat karena libur. Namun, tolong tetap cek email kalian.

resources.title: Contrasting ideas: 'although', 'despite' and others
resources.note: A B1–B2 grammar page on although, even though and though + subject + verb, with two short tests. It also teaches despite and in spite of (+ noun), which go beyond this lesson, and it doesn't cover however, reasons or purpose.

id.note: Halaman tata bahasa B1–B2 tentang although, even though dan though + subjek + kata kerja, dengan dua tes singkat. Halaman ini juga mengajarkan despite dan in spite of (+ kata benda), yang di luar pelajaran ini, dan tidak membahas however, alasan atau tujuan.

id.intro: Kamu sudah bisa menghubungkan ide dengan **but**, **because** dan **so**. Di pelajaran ini kamu akan terdengar lebih dewasa di email, laporan dan percakapan: **although** dan **however** untuk hal yang mengejutkan (kontras), **because of** dan **due to** untuk alasan, serta **to**, **in order to** dan **so that** untuk tujuan. Pemanasan: kenapa kamu belajar bahasa Inggris? Lanjutkan kalimat ini: I'm learning English so that I can … (Saya belajar bahasa Inggris supaya saya bisa …)
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa aku tidak boleh bilang 'Although …, but …'?
Kapan pakai because dan kapan because of?
Apa bedanya so dan so that?

assessment.lcp-1: Pertahankan although dan perbaiki kesalahannya: Although the hotel was expensive, but the room was small and dirty.
assessment.lcp-2: Tulis although atau however: The apartment is near my office. ___, the rent is very high.
assessment.lcp-3: Tulis because atau because of: Dimas missed the meeting ___ a problem with his laptop.
assessment.lcp-4: Perbaiki kesalahannya: Because of the KRL was late, I missed the meeting.
assessment.lcp-5: Pengumuman bandara butuh kata yang lebih formal. Tulis ulang kalimatnya dengan due to: The flight to Bali is late because the weather is bad.
assessment.lcp-6: Pertahankan kata kerja buy dan perbaiki kesalahannya: Rina is saving money for buy a new motorbike.
assessment.lcp-7: Isi titik-titiknya dengan so that + subjek + can: Budi leaves home at 5 a.m. ___ catch the first KRL.
